tasks.title: Wire consent gate into analytics.js, gtm.js, and inline gtag snippets
tasks.success: analytics.js's gtag('config', ...) call and gtm.js's gtm.init() call only run when consent is 'accepted'; the inline gtag bootstrap snippets in index.html and contact.html are wrapped the same way.
tasks.verify: Read the modified files to confirm the gate wraps every tracking init path; dev-server smoke test that rejecting consent prevents network calls to googletagmanager.com.
tasks.notes: analytics.js/gtm.js now check localStorage('wo_cookie_consent') directly (robust to script load order) and also listen for 'wo:cookie-consent'. Discovered index.html additionally had a raw inline gtag.js snippet AND a raw inline GTM bootstrap snippet AND a static no-JS GTM noscript iframe that were NOT gated and duplicated what gtm.js/analytics.js already do - removed all three from index.html and the inline gtag snippet from contact.html, since they were firing unconditionally regardless of consent. This closes a real gap the original design doc didn't anticipate (the actual bootstrap lived partly in raw HTML, not just in the two JS files) and removes pre-existing double-loading of GA/GTM. No other code calls gtag()/dataLayer before analytics.js runs (grepped), so this is safe. Browser smoke test deferred to T7 alongside the banner check.

tasks.notes: Script updated 35 files; index.html and contact.html false-positive-skipped (matched the string in a code comment from T6) so added by hand. All 39 live pages now include cookie-consent.js. Ran a real Playwright smoke test against parcel dev server: banner shows on first visit, zero googletagmanager.com requests before consent, Accept triggers gtm.js+gtag.js load and persists 'accepted' in localStorage, Reject persists 'rejected' and blocks tracking even after reload, banner never reappears once a choice is made.
